topic: React and Next.js for FDE demos and internal tools
why: The customer never sees your FastAPI service, your Temporal workflows or your eval harness; they see a screen, and in week two of every engagement someone asks 'can you put a UI on that so the ops team can use it'. An FDE who can stand up a typed, authenticated, streaming Next.js front end over their own API in an afternoon turns a backend demo into a pilot the customer can click through, and can also read and fix the customer's existing Next.js code (most enterprise platform teams already run it). Take-homes at Palantir, Anthropic and Databricks routinely include a small UI, and the difference between a screen that streams tokens through the customer's Nginx and one that freezes for eight seconds is exactly the kind of production detail this topic drills.
prerequisites: TypeScript at the level of topic 28 (TypeScript and Node for FDEs): generics, discriminated unions, `satisfies`, async iteration, ESM vs CJS, `tsc --noEmit` in CI
A running DefenderMate backend from topics 26, 27 and 32: a token or OIDC login endpoint, at least one JSON list/detail endpoint, and an SSE endpoint relaying Claude's event stream
HTTP mechanics from topics 2 and 32: cookies and SameSite, CORS preflight, chunked transfer encoding, the SSE frame format, and where reverse proxies buffer
Auth from topic 27: verifying an RS256 JWT against a JWKS URL, refresh-token rotation, tenant claims, CSRF and why httpOnly cookies beat localStorage
Docker multi-stage builds and non-root images from topic 6, plus an Nginx or ALB in the path from topics 13 and 16 so streaming can be tested realistically
Node 20.9+ and pnpm or npm installed; working HTML/CSS basics (semantic elements, native form controls, flex and grid)

subtopics.name: React rendering model: state ownership, derived values, keys
subtopics.learn: Walk through render -> commit -> browser paint and be able to say, for any screen in an internal tool (run list, run detail, streaming answer pane), which component owns each piece of state and which values are derived and must not live in `useState`. Practise 'lifting state up' and 'colocating state' on the DefenderMate run list: filter text lives in the list component, the selected run ID lives in the parent, the streaming buffer lives next to the reader. Know why `key` must be a stable identity (run ID, never array index) for lists that reorder or stream in, and what breaks when it is not: preserved input state on the wrong row, lost focus, remounted children.

subtopics.name: Effects only for external systems: subscriptions, aborts, StrictMode double-invoke
subtopics.learn: Adopt the rule that `useEffect` exists to synchronise with something outside React (an EventSource, a WebSocket, a timer, the DOM) and never to compute derived data or respond to a prop change. Write the canonical fetch-in-effect correctly once: create an `AbortController`, pass `signal`, return a cleanup that aborts, and watch `StrictMode` mount-unmount-mount in dev prove your cleanup works. Understand the race where two rapid selections resolve out of order and how the abort or an `ignore` flag in cleanup fixes it. Know when `useSyncExternalStore` replaces an effect-plus-state pair for external stores.

resource.label: react.dev - You Might Not Need an Effect

subtopics.name: Server and Client Components: what the boundary actually is
subtopics.learn: Internalise that `'use client'` marks a module boundary, not a place where code 'runs only in the browser': everything imported from a client module is bundled to the browser and still server-rendered to HTML once. Server Components can be async, read `cookies()`/`headers()`, hold secrets, and never re-render; props crossing the boundary must be serialisable (plain objects, arrays, Date, Map, Set, Promises, Server Functions; no class instances, no event handlers). Master the composition pattern: a client `<Tabs>` receives server-rendered `children`, so interactivity does not force data fetching into the browser. Add `import 'server-only'` to every module that touches tokens or the FastAPI base URL so a client import fails at build time rather than leaking at runtime, and check the Network tab to see what the RSC payload actually contains.

resource.label: Next.js docs - Server and Client Components

subtopics.name: App Router file conventions: layouts, pages, dynamic segments, async params
subtopics.learn: Know exactly what each file does: `layout.tsx` (persists across navigations, does not re-render, cannot read `searchParams`), `page.tsx`, `loading.tsx` (an automatic Suspense boundary), `error.tsx`, `not-found.tsx`, `route.ts`, and route groups `(admin)` for grouping without a URL segment. Since Next 15 `params` and `searchParams` are Promises: `const { id } = await params` in `app/runs/[id]/page.tsx`, with the generated `PageProps<'/runs/[id]'>` type from `next typegen` giving you typed segments. Build the shell for DefenderMate: `app/(app)/layout.tsx` with nav and auth check, `app/(app)/runs/page.tsx`, `app/(app)/runs/[id]/page.tsx`, `app/login/page.tsx`, and use `<Link>` prefetching plus `useRouter().refresh()` deliberately, not by accident.

subtopics.name: Fetching from FastAPI inside Server Components: auth forwarding, parallelism, typed responses
subtopics.learn: Fetch DefenderMate from the server with the session cookie translated into `Authorization: Bearer` inside a `server-only` API client, and know that Next's `fetch` default is 'auto no cache' (request-time unless you opt in with `cache: 'force-cache'` or `next: { revalidate, tags }`). Avoid waterfalls: start independent requests before awaiting (`const runsP = getRuns(); const statsP = getStats(); const [runs, stats] = await Promise.all([runsP, statsP])`), and use the preload pattern for data a child needs. Throw on `!res.ok` with the status and a redacted body so `error.tsx` catches it. Generate response types from the FastAPI OpenAPI document (`openapi-typescript`) so a schema change in topic 35's contract tests also fails `tsc` here; never hand-write the run model twice.

subtopics.name: Streaming the page: Suspense boundaries, loading.tsx, and use()
subtopics.learn: Understand that the App Router streams one HTTP response: the shell renders immediately and each `<Suspense fallback>` island is filled in as its promise resolves, in the same response body, so headers (including redirects and cookies) cannot be changed after the first flush. Place boundaries where latency actually differs: the run header is fast, the Claude-generated summary is slow, so wrap only the summary. Pass a promise from a Server Component to a Client Component and unwrap it with `use(promise)` when the client needs to own the pending state. Size fallbacks to the final content to avoid layout shift, and test with a throttled FastAPI endpoint (`await asyncio.sleep(3)`) to see the streaming order in the Network waterfall.

subtopics.name: Cache Components: use cache, cacheLife, cacheTag, updateTag
subtopics.learn: Learn the Next 16 model: with `cacheComponents: true` in `next.config.ts`, nothing is cached unless you say so and any request-time data (`cookies()`, `headers()`, `searchParams`, uncached `fetch`) must sit under a Suspense boundary or the build fails with an 'uncached data accessed outside Suspense' error. Mark a function or component with `'use cache'`, set its lifetime with `cacheLife('minutes' | 'hours' | 'days' | 'max')` or a custom profile, label it with `cacheTag('runs')`, and after a mutation call `updateTag('runs')` (read-your-own-writes in the same request) or `revalidateTag('runs', 'max')` for stale-while-revalidate. Use `connection()` when you need to force request-time rendering without reading a dynamic API. Know which of the DefenderMate screens should be cached at all: reference data yes, a tenant's run list no.

resource.label: Next.js docs - Caching and Revalidating (Cache Components)

subtopics.name: Route Handlers as the backend-for-frontend, including streaming pass-through
subtopics.learn: Write `app/api/runs/[id]/stream/route.ts` exporting `GET(request: NextRequest, ctx: RouteContext<'/api/runs/[id]/stream'>)` that reads the session cookie, calls FastAPI with `Authorization: Bearer`, and returns `new Response(upstream.body, { headers })` with `Content-Type: text/event-stream`, `Cache-Control: no-cache, no-transform` and `X-Accel-Buffering: no`. Set `export const dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`, `runtime = 'nodejs'` and `maxDuration` appropriately. Pass `request.signal` to the upstream `fetch` and verify with FastAPI logs that closing the tab stops the Claude generation within a second; if your Next version does not propagate the abort, wrap the upstream in a `ReadableStream` whose `cancel()` aborts an `AbortController`. Know why the BFF exists at all: the browser never holds the API token, CORS disappears, and the customer's SSO cookie stays first-party.

resource.label: Next.js docs - Backend for Frontend guide

subtopics.name: Consuming the token stream in a Client Component without melting the UI
subtopics.learn: Read the Route Handler stream with `fetch` plus `res.body.pipeThrough(new TextDecoderStream()).getReader()` and parse SSE frames yourself: split on blank lines, carry partial lines across chunks in a buffer, dispatch on `event:` (DefenderMate relays Claude's `content_block_delta`, `message_stop`, error events from topic 32) and parse `data:` as JSON. Tie an `AbortController` to both component unmount and a Stop button. Do not `setState` per token: append to a ref and flush at most once per animation frame or via `startTransition`, or the 40 re-renders per second stall typing in the input. Know why `EventSource` is a poor fit here (GET only, no custom headers, but cookie auth does work) and when its automatic reconnect with `Last-Event-ID` is still worth it.

subtopics.name: Forms with Server Functions, Zod 4 validation, useActionState and useOptimistic
subtopics.learn: Write `'use server'` functions that receive `FormData`, parse it with Zod 4 (`schema.safeParse(Object.fromEntries(formData))`, `z.flattenError` for field errors) and return a `{ errors, values }` state object; wire it with `useActionState(action, initialState)` to get `[state, formAction, isPending]` and render field errors next to inputs. Prove progressive enhancement by disabling JavaScript: the form still submits and the errors still render because the action is a plain POST. Use `useFormStatus()` in a child submit button, `useOptimistic` to add the new run to the list instantly and roll back on failure, and `redirect()` after success (never inside try/catch: it throws). Call `updateTag`/`revalidateTag` in the action so the list is fresh on the next render.

subtopics.name: Server Functions are public POST endpoints: authorisation, arguments, CSRF, size limits
subtopics.learn: Treat every Server Function as an unauthenticated HTTP endpoint identified by an action ID visible in the Network tab: authorise inside the function (`const session = await verifySession()`), validate every argument (the client can send anything), and never trust that 'only admins see the button'. Know that closure-captured values are encrypted with a build-time key and that multi-replica deployments need `NEXT_SERVER_ACTIONS_ENCRYPTION_KEY` set consistently or actions fail after a rolling deploy. Configure `serverActions.allowedOrigins` when a reverse proxy makes `Origin` differ from `Host` (Next's built-in CSRF check compares them), and `serverActions.bodySizeLimit` (default 1 MB) before a file-upload form silently 413s in the customer's environment.

subtopics.name: Auth: session cookie, Data Access Layer, JWKS verification against FastAPI
subtopics.learn: Implement login as a Server Function that posts credentials (or completes the OIDC code exchange from topic 27) to FastAPI, then `(await cookies()).set('session', token, { httpOnly: true, secure: true, sameSite: 'lax', path: '/', expires })`; cookies can only be set in Server Functions and Route Handlers, not in Server Components. Build a `server-only` Data Access Layer with `verifySession()` wrapped in React `cache()` so it runs once per request, verifying the JWT with `jose` (`jwtVerify` against `createRemoteJWKSet(new URL(issuer + '/.well-known/jwks.json'))`, checking `iss`, `aud`, `exp` and the tenant claim) and returning a DTO with only the fields the UI needs. Every data function calls the DAL; layouts are not a security boundary because they do not re-render on navigation. Handle refresh-token rotation and logout (`cookies().delete`) and confirm a tampered cookie yields a redirect to `/login`, never a stack trace.

subtopics.name: proxy.ts (formerly middleware): matchers, optimistic redirects, request headers
subtopics.learn: Write `proxy.ts` at the project root exporting `default function proxy(request: NextRequest)` with `export const config = { matcher: ['/((?!api|_next/static|_next/image|favicon.ico).*)'] }` so it skips static assets. In Next 16 it runs on the Node.js runtime by default but still executes on every matched request before the cache, so keep it cheap: check cookie presence for an optimistic redirect to `/login`, stamp `x-request-id` and tenant headers onto the request with `NextResponse.next({ request: { headers } })`, and rewrite for A/B or maintenance pages. Do not verify JWTs or call databases here; the DAL is the real check. Know the middleware-to-proxy migration so you can read customer codebases on either name.

subtopics.name: Error boundaries, digests, not-found, and redaction in production
subtopics.learn: `error.tsx` must be a Client Component receiving `{ error: Error & { digest?: string }, reset: () => void }`; in production Next redacts server error messages and ships only a `digest`, which you must log server-side to correlate. `global-error.tsx` replaces the root layout and must render `<html>` and `<body>` itself. Call `notFound()` for a missing run so the segment's `not-found.tsx` renders with a 404. Errors thrown after streaming has started become inline error boundaries, not HTTP 500s, so monitor them via `instrumentation.ts` `onRequestError(err, request, context)` rather than status codes. Put a 'copy digest' button in your error UI so a customer screenshot is enough to find the log line.

subtopics.name: OpenTelemetry from Next.js into your FastAPI traces
subtopics.learn: Add `instrumentation.ts` with `export function register()` that calls `registerOTel({ serviceName: 'defendermate-ui' })` from `@vercel/otel` (or a manual `NodeSDK` guarded by `process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs'`), export to the same collector as topic 21, and read Next's built-in spans: `BaseServer.handleRequest`, `AppRender.getBodyResult`, `AppRouteRouteHandlers.runHandler`, `AppRender.fetch`. Confirm `traceparent` is propagated on the server-side `fetch` to FastAPI so one trace spans page render, BFF hop and Claude call; set `NEXT_OTEL_VERBOSE=1` when you need per-component spans. Implement `onRequestError` to record the digest, route, and `renderSource` on the active span so a digest-to-trace lookup is one query.

subtopics.name: Internal-tool UI kit: Tailwind v4, shadcn/ui, TanStack Table, accessibility
subtopics.learn: Do not design a component library on a customer's clock: `npx shadcn@latest init` then `add button input table dialog form` copies accessible components (over Radix or Base UI primitives) into `components/ui` that you own and can edit. Tailwind v4 is CSS-first (`@import "tailwindcss"` and `@theme {}` tokens, no `tailwind.config.js` by default); use the `cn()` helper for conditional classes. Build the runs table with TanStack Table `useReactTable({ data, columns, getCoreRowModel, manualPagination: true, pageCount })` driven by `searchParams` (`?page=2&sort=created_at.desc`) so every view is a shareable URL and pagination happens in FastAPI, not the browser. Keep native `<label htmlFor>`, focus rings and `aria-live="polite"` on the streaming pane; load heavy widgets (charts, code editors) with `next/dynamic` and check `@next/bundle-analyzer` before the demo.

subtopics.name: TanStack Query where it earns its place: polling, mutations, hydration
subtopics.learn: Use TanStack Query v5 only for client-owned data: polling a running agent with `useQuery({ queryKey: ['run', id], queryFn, refetchInterval: (q) => q.state.data?.status === 'running' ? 1000 : false })`, `useMutation` with `onSuccess: () => queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ['runs'] })`, and `staleTime` tuned so navigation does not refetch. Prefetch on the server with `queryClient.prefetchQuery` and hand it to the client via `<HydrationBoundary state={dehydrate(queryClient)}>` so there is no double fetch after hydration. Create the `QueryClient` per request on the server (an `isServer` check in a `getQueryClient()` helper) and once per browser on the client via `useState(() => new QueryClient())`; a module-level client on the server leaks one user's cache to the next request.

resource.label: TanStack Query docs - Advanced Server Rendering (App Router)

subtopics.name: Hydration mismatches: dates, locales, window checks, extensions
subtopics.learn:
Know the causes cold: `new Date().toLocaleString()` rendered on a UTC server and a local-time client, `Math.random()` or `crypto.randomUUID()` in render, `typeof window !== 'undefined'` branches that change output, invalid HTML nesting (`
` inside `

`), and browser extensions that mutate the DOM before hydration. Fixes: render timestamps with a fixed timezone or format them in a Client Component after mount, use `useId()` for IDs, `useSyncExternalStore(subscribe, getSnapshot, getServerSnapshot)` for client-only values like `matchMedia`, and `suppressHydrationWarning` only on the single text node that legitimately differs. Understand that a mismatch makes React 19 throw away the server HTML and re-render on the client, so the page 'works' but pays full client-render cost and floods the console the customer's security team is watching.

subtopics.name: Shipping to a customer VPC: runtime env, standalone Docker, Nginx, skew
subtopics.learn: Understand that `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` is inlined at `next build`, so one image cannot carry different API URLs per environment; read environment-specific values on the server only (in the DAL or a Route Handler) and pass what the browser needs as props. Build with `output: 'standalone'`: a multi-stage Dockerfile that copies `.next/standalone`, `.next/static` and `public`, runs `node server.js` as a non-root user with `HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0` and `PORT`, and installs `sharp` for image optimisation. In front of Nginx, send `X-Accel-Buffering: no` (via `headers()` in `next.config.ts` or on the streaming response) and know that `next start`'s built-in `compress` can buffer SSE, so set `compress: false` and compress at the proxy. Set `deploymentId` so clients holding old HTML during a rolling deploy do not hit `ChunkLoadError`, and configure a shared `cacheHandler` (Redis, topic 31) when you run more than one replica with cached segments.

subtopics.name: Testing the UI: Playwright e2e with storageState, Vitest for client components, build as a gate
subtopics.learn: Write Playwright tests that log in once in a setup project and reuse `storageState`, then assert the real behaviours: the runs table renders rows from a seeded FastAPI, the stream pane accumulates text (`await expect(page.getByTestId('answer')).toContainText('...', { timeout: 30_000 })`), Stop cancels the request, and the form shows field errors with `javaScriptEnabled: false`. Use Vitest plus Testing Library for pure Client Components only; Next documents that async Server Components are not supported by Vitest, so cover them end to end. Make `tsc --noEmit`, `next typegen` and `next build` the CI gate and read the build route table (static vs dynamic markers) as a review artifact; run the Playwright suite against the built container, not `next dev`.

outcomes: You can scaffold a Next 16 App Router app and, in under two hours, ship a typed list/detail UI over an existing FastAPI service with server-side fetching, a `loading.tsx` skeleton and an `error.tsx` boundary, with `next build` passing type-check and showing each route's static/dynamic marker.

You can draw the server/client boundary for a given screen on a whiteboard, naming which components are Server Components, which are `'use client'`, exactly what crosses the boundary as props, and where the secret-bearing fetch runs, and justify each choice in one sentence.

You can stream Claude output from DefenderMate through a Route Handler to a Client Component with a working Stop button, show in FastAPI logs that the upstream generation stops within one second of abort, and demonstrate it working behind a default-config Nginx after adding the documented headers.

You can implement login as a Server Function that sets an httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Lax session cookie, gate every data fetch through a `server-only` Data Access Layer that verifies the JWT with `jose` against FastAPI's JWKS, and show that a missing cookie redirects and a tampered cookie yields a clean redirect, never a stack trace or a digest.

You can validate a form with Zod 4 on the server via `useActionState`, render field-level errors with JavaScript disabled, and show `useOptimistic` updating the list before the server responds and rolling back on failure.

You can explain the Cache Components model and demonstrate `'use cache'` plus `cacheTag` plus `updateTag` fixing a stale dashboard after a mutation, and reproduce the build error you get when request-time data is read outside a Suspense boundary.

You can build one standalone Docker image that runs unchanged in staging and prod with no `NEXT_PUBLIC_` environment leakage, runs as non-root, and passes a Playwright smoke test executed against the container in CI.
You can take an `error.digest` from a customer screenshot, find the matching `onRequestError` log line, and follow the propagated `traceparent` into the FastAPI span in the trace backend.
failureModes: The customer's Nginx (and `next start`'s own gzip layer) buffered the SSE stream so the whole answer appeared after eight seconds; the demo looked broken until `X-Accel-Buffering: no` was sent and `compress: false` moved compression to the proxy.

`NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL` was baked into the image at build time pointing at staging; the production demo silently showed staging data, and the 'fix' of rebuilding per environment destroyed the one-image-everywhere reproducibility the customer's platform team required.

An admin 'delete tenant' Server Function had no authorisation inside the function because 'only admins see the button'; anyone who copied the action ID from the Network tab could POST it, and it was found in the customer's pentest.

A dashboard showed yesterday's numbers because the fetch sat inside `'use cache'` with `cacheLife('days')` and the mutation only called `revalidatePath`, which never touched the tag; the customer concluded the ingestion pipeline was down.

`new Date().toLocaleString()` rendered in server UTC and client local time caused a hydration mismatch on every page; React discarded the SSR tree and re-rendered client-side, adding a visible flash and a wall of console errors that the customer's security reviewer logged as a finding.

A rolling deploy without `deploymentId` left open tabs requesting chunk hashes that no longer existed, so every user in the customer's morning stand-up hit `ChunkLoadError` at once and the FDE was paged from the meeting.

A module-level `new QueryClient()` imported by a Server Component was shared across requests on one pod, so user A briefly saw user B's cached run list; it passed every test because the e2e suite ran a single user.
interviewQuestions: Draw the request lifecycle for an authenticated dashboard page in the App Router: browser, proxy.ts, layout, page, Data Access Layer, FastAPI, RSC payload. Where does the JWT live at each hop, and where exactly do you enforce that a user only sees their own tenant's runs, and why not in the layout?

A customer says streaming works on the engineer's laptop but in their Kubernetes cluster the answer appears all at once after eight seconds. Walk me through localising the buffering hop across the Client Component, the Route Handler, `next start`, the ingress and the FastAPI pod, and the specific change at each.

For a run-monitoring screen, when do you fetch in a Server Component versus a Route Handler versus TanStack Query in a Client Component versus a Server Function? Defend the split and explain how you avoid a double fetch after hydration.

Explain what `'use client'` actually does to a module graph. A colleague added it to the root layout to fix a `useState` error and the bundle tripled. What happened, and how do you restructure with the composition pattern?

Design forms for an internal tool at a customer whose corporate proxy sometimes strips JavaScript and enforces a strict CSP: progressive enhancement, validation, error display, optimistic updates, and the CSRF story for Server Functions behind a reverse proxy where `Origin` and `Host` differ.

We ship one Docker image to five customer environments with different API URLs and SSO issuers. How do you configure a Next.js app at runtime without rebuilding, what breaks if you rely on `NEXT_PUBLIC_`, and how do you keep Server Functions working across replicas and deploys?

After a deploy, 5 percent of users see 'Application error: a server-side exception has occurred' with a digest. Walk me from that digest to root cause, and tell me what you would add so the next incident is self-explanatory from a single customer screenshot.
proofOfWork: A recorded ten-minute 'customer demo' plus a public repo that a platform team could clone and run. The repo contains the Next 16 app over DefenderMate built as a standalone, non-root Docker image behind an Nginx container with default settings; a one-page architecture diagram in the README marking the server/client boundary, the session-cookie auth flow through the Data Access Layer, and the streaming path from Claude to the browser; a `docs/streaming-drill.md` with before/after HAR captures showing the buffered stream and the fix (headers and `compress: false`); a `docs/runtime-config.md` proving the same image digest runs against two different FastAPI base URLs and issuers without rebuilding; a Playwright suite (login via `storageState`, table pagination via URL, stream with Stop asserting the FastAPI log line for the aborted generation, form validation with `javaScriptEnabled: false`) running in GitHub Actions against the built container; and a `docs/digest-to-trace.md` walkthrough with screenshots going from an `error.digest` in the UI to the `onRequestError` log entry to the trace in the collector that includes the FastAPI span, so a customer support engineer could repeat the lookup unaided.
